chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is half the dower, if something was obligated for her; and if it was not obligated for her, then let him provide for her with provision in the manner that he would provide for similar women.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or he should relinquish in whose hand is the marriage tie.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the father, or the brother, and the man who has been bequeathed to it, and the man whose instructions are allowed in the wealth of the woman, so he buys for her and sells for her. So when he excuses, it is allowed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower and provision for a woman divorced before consummation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the financial entitlements of a woman divorced before consummation, distinguishing between cases where a specific dower was agreed upon versus those requiring discretionary provision (muta'). It further elucidates the Quranic phrase 'in whose hand is the marriage tie' to include not only the husband but also the father, brother, or guardian who holds authority over her affairs, reflecting the Shia understanding of marital guardianship.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who divorces his wife before he sleeps with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is half the dower, if something was Obligated for her; and if it was not Obligated for her, so let him provide for her approximately to what he would provide for the likes of her from the women’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And heasws said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:237] or he should relinquish in whose hand is the marriage tie. Heasws said: ‘He is the father, or the brother, and the man who has been bequeathed to it, and the man whose instructions are allowed in the wealth of the woman, so he buys for her and he sells for her. So when he excuses, so it is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who divorces his wife before going to bed with her, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘He owes to her one-half of mahr (dower) if he has set something for her; but if he has not set anything for her he must benefit her like the benefits that similar women receive. 5

The words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, say, ‘. . . or it is waived by the one who has authority in the matters of marriage. . .’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Of such people is father, or a brother or the executor of the will or a man who is authorized in dealing with the assets of the woman to buy for her and he buys if he waves, it then is effective.
